subjective.chief_complaint: Pruritic, sore rash of the skin (chest, hands, inner elbows) started about 3–4 days ago.
subjective.hpi: Patient reports a very itchy, dry, cracked red rash on the chest, hands, and inner elbows for about 3–4 days. It is affecting sleep and concentration at work. Previously had eczema; used OTC steroid cream yesterday without relief. No fever or systemic symptoms. Denies new exposures, changes in shower gels, or clothing. No facial involvement. No bleeding or discharge observed. Bowel and urinary functions normal.
ros: Pruritus on chest, hands, and inner elbows
No fever, cough, dyspnea, or chest symptoms
No bleeding or discharge from skin
social_history: Occasional alcohol use (few beers per week)

physical_exam.skin: Itchy, dry, cracked rash described on chest, hands, and inner elbows; no facial involvement; skin cracking noted; no bleeding or discharge observed; no signs of acute infection described

assessment.summary: Pruritic, dry, cracked dermatitis with distribution on chest, hands, and inner elbows in the setting of prior eczema.

actions: Prescribe topical corticosteroid cream (strong prescription) for short course
Prescribe emollients/moisturizers for regular use in bath/shower
Advise patient diary to track potential triggers (shower gels/soaps, detergents, clothing)
monitoring: Assess response to therapy in 7–10 days
Monitor for adverse effects of topical steroids
Advise return sooner if symptoms worsen or signs of infection develop
plan.patient_instructions: Apply emollients daily; use topical corticosteroid as prescribed for 7–10 days; take fexofenadine as directed; maintain a diary of potential triggers and product exposures; return for re-evaluation if not improved in 1 week or if symptoms worsen.
